job.title: Business Development Officer
job.description:
Business Development Officer (Casual Contract) Melbourne CBD | 12 Hours Per Week | 12-Week Casual Assignment

Are you an energetic and confident communicator who enjoys connecting with people and creating new business opportunities? We're looking for a proactive Business Development Officer to join our team on a short-term casual basis and support our business growth initiatives.

This role is ideal for someone with strong outbound sales experience, excellent computer skills, and a passion for prospecting and relationship building.

About the Role Working closely with our leadership team, you will play a key role in identifying and engaging potential clients within the staffing and workforce solutions market. Your primary focus will be cleansing and maintaining prospect data, conducting outbound calls and email campaigns, and securing appointments for our sales team.

Working Arrangement
  • 12 hours per week
  • Casual contract for 12 weeks
  • 4 hours per day (open to 2 x 6 hour days for experienced candidates)
  • Tuesday & Thursday: Melbourne CBD office
  • Wednesday: Work from Home
Key Responsibilities
  • Cleanse, update, and maintain prospect and customer data within our CRM system
  • Research and identify target organisations and decision-makers
  • Conduct outbound calls to prospective clients
  • Create and send tailored prospecting emails and follow-up communications
  • Book qualified appointments for senior sales representatives
  • Maintain accurate records of all sales activities and interactions
  • Support lead generation and business development campaigns
  • Provide regular reporting on activity levels and outcomes
About You We're looking for someone who is commercially minded, organised, and comfortable engaging with senior decision-makers.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Previous experience in outbound sales, telemarketing, appointment setting, business development, or lead generation
  • Strong confidence on the phone with excellent communication skills
  • High level of computer literacy and experience using CRM systems
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when managing and cleansing data
  • Ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively
  • Professional and resilient approach to prospecting and follow-up
Desirable (but not essential)
  • Experience within staffing, recruitment, workforce planning, labour hire, or professional services
  • Understanding of recruitment and workforce solutions markets
What We Offer
  • Flexible hybrid working arrangement
  • Modern Melbourne CBD office location
  • Opportunity to contribute directly to business growth
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Potential for future opportunities based on performance
If you're a motivated sales professional who enjoys generating opportunities and building pipelines through proactive outreach, we'd love to hear from you.

Follow the prompts and apply online today. 

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Support Needs Assessors
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Support Needs Assessors to join a Federal Government client on a full-time contract. In this role, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred assessments, working directly with participants to identify and articulate their support needs in a clear, evidence-based and respectful manner.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct support needs assessments with participants and their representatives
  • Analyse information and external evidence to support sound, evidence-based decisions
  • Prepare clear, accurate assessment reports
  • Communicate assessment processes and outcomes clearly (virtual and face-to-face)
  • Apply relevant policies, procedures and legislative frameworks
  • Identify and escalate complex or high-risk matters
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support participant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records using case management systems
  • Adapt assessment approaches to suit individual participant needs
About You You will bring:

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience in assessment, interviewing or case management
  • Ability to interpret evidence and provide clear, defensible recommendations
  • A commitment to person-centred, inclusive and trauma-informed practice
  • Sound judgement, professionalism and ethical integrity
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Experience working within or knowledge of NDIS or similar frameworks (highly regarded)
Essential Requirements
  • Recognised tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, such as:

    • Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech Pathology
    • Social Work, Counselling, Psychology/Psychotherapy
    • Exercise Physiology, Dietetics, Rehabilitation Counselling
    • Nursing (RN/EN), Education-qualified clinicians
    • NDIS Behaviour Support Practitioner
  • Experience in support needs assessments or similar frameworks

  • Understanding of person-centred and strengths-based approaches

For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com 

If you fit the above criteria we would love to hear from you, APPLY now!

job.title: Participant Support Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for multiple Business Support Officer opportunities. This is a rewarding role where you'll play an important part in supporting participants through key stages of their journey, delivering quality customer service and helping to achieve positive outcomes.
Working within a collaborative and fast-paced environment, you will manage a variety of administrative, operational and customer-focused tasks while engaging with participants, providers and stakeholders across Australia. This a full time, office based, labour hire contract.

About the Role As a Participant Support Officer, you'll be responsible for managing a diverse workload, resolving enquiries, and supporting participants through established processes and pathways. You'll use a range of systems and tools to review information, assess participant matters, and ensure actions are completed accurately and within required timeframes.

This role requires strong judgement, empathy, attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage participant-related enquiries and provide accurate information and support.
  • Conduct reviews of participant information and maintain records across multiple systems.
  • Make outbound calls to participants, providers and stakeholders to gather information and progress matters.
  • Assess and action participant requests in line with legislation, policies and operational guidelines.
  • Escalate complex issues where required and contribute to achieving team service delivery outcomes.
  • Assist with process improvements, reporting activities and project-related initiatives.
  • Work collaboratively with team members to share knowledge, provide feedback and support continuous improvement.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport and engage with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service experience within a high-volume environment.
  • The ability to remain calm, professional and solution-focused when dealing with sensitive or complex situations.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • A high level of attention to detail when working with data and documentation.
  • Experience interpreting policies, procedures or legislative frameworks.
  • Confidence using Microsoft Office and navigating multiple systems simultaneously.
What We're Looking For
  • Experience in administration, customer service, contact centres, case management, human services, health, government or community services environments.
  • Ability to handle sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated resilience, adaptability and commitment to delivering positive customer outcomes.
  • A collaborative team player with a proactive approach to learning and continuous improvement.
For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com

If you match the above criteria APPLY now

job.title: Order Picker
job.description:
Order Pickers – Chiller, Freezer & Ambient Areas

Location: Larapinta & Heathwood, QLD
Employment Type: Casual | Flexible Shifts | Must Be Available 24/7
Pay Rate: Starting from $39/hour + penalties 

We are seeking expressions of interest from experienced and dynamic Order Pickers to join our client’s busy Distribution Centre in Larapinta & Heathwood. This is a fantastic opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment with a safety-driven team and excellent onsite management.

What You’ll Be Doing
  • Voice-pick orders accurately and efficiently
  • Operate electronic pallet transporters (tuggers)
  • Palletise orders and navigate the facility on foot and transporters
  • Perform manual handling tasks (lifting up to 20kg)
What We’re Looking For
  • Strong team player with a positive attitude
  • Excellent work ethic and initiative
  • Safety-conscious and reliable
  • Good communication skills (verbal & written)
  • Physically fit – on your feet all day
  • Previous experience in a large distribution centre (advantageous)
  • Previous experience in chiller or freezer distribution centres 
  • Hands-on approach and flexibility for varied tasks
Essential Requirements
  • Own car and valid driver’s licence
  • Experience with electronic pallet transporters and order picking
  • Ability to work up to 10-hour shifts and 38 hours per week (including weekends & public holidays)
  • Willingness to undergo a full medical (including drug & alcohol screening) and national police check
Don’t miss out on this fantastic opportunity!

Click APPLY now and submit your resume.

job.title: Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
job.description:
Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
Kurri Kurri, NSW
Attractive Salary Package

Our client is seeking an experienced and results-driven Project Manager to join their Project Delivery team based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of sustaining and capital projects across mobile delivery systems, infrastructure upgrades, commissioning activities, asset mobilisation, and operational improvement initiatives.

About the Role Reporting to the Lead Projects, you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of multiple projects, ensuring outcomes are achieved safely, on time, within budget, and to the highest standards.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing multiple sustaining and capital projects simultaneously.
  • Developing project scopes, schedules, budgets, and risk management plans.
  • Coordinating contractors, suppliers, procurement activities, and project resources.
  • Managing project governance, reporting, forecasting, and project controls.
  • Leading mobilisation, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Driving projects through to successful completion while balancing competing priorities.
About You
We are looking for a practical project professional with a strong delivery focus and the ability to navigate complexity.

You may come from a background in:
  • Project Delivery
  • Mining
  • Fixed Plant or Mobile Equipment
  • Civil Construction
  • Heavy Manufacturing
  • Maintenance and Shutdowns
  • Operations or Logistics
  • Trades or Construction Supervision
While engineering qualifications may be beneficial, this is not a design engineering role. We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully coordinated and delivered projects within operational, maintenance, construction, or manufacturing environments. Formal project management qualifications will be highly regarded.

What Will Make You Successful

The ideal candidate will:
  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information.
  • Thrive in ambiguous and changing environments.
  • Balance competing stakeholder expectations.
  • Drive outcomes despite uncertainty.
  • Maintain strong ownership and accountability.
  • Be highly organised and capable of managing multiple projects concurrently.
  • Hold stakeholders accountable and follow through on commitments.
  • Focus on delivering practical outcomes rather than pursuing technical perfection.
In short, we're looking for someone who can bring structure to complexity, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and consistently deliver successful project outcomes.

Key Requirements
  • 5+ years' experience managing capital and/or sustaining projects.
  • Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Strong contractor management and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and risk.
  • Excellent communication, planning, and organisational skills.
  • Experience working within industrial, manufacturing, mining, maintenance, or construction environments.
What's on Offer
  • Attractive salary package.
  • Opportunity to manage a diverse portfolio of projects with significant business impact.
  • Supportive and collaborative project delivery environment.
  • Minimal travel requirements (less than 10%).
  • Based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.
If you're a proactive Project Manager who enjoys creating order from complexity, influencing stakeholders, and delivering outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Production Operator
job.description:
Production Operator
We are seeking reliable and motivated Production Operator to join our manufacturing client based in Beverley. This is a hands-on role working within a production environment, supporting the efficient operation of the product fill line and maintaining high-quality standards.
This position offers a Monday to Friday roster, with rotating day and afternoon shifts. Occasional weekend work may be required to meet production demands. You'll rotate through a variety of production tasks, providing plenty of variety throughout your workday while contributing to a safe and productive workplace.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Rotate through various production and fill line tasks
  • Load buckets and lids onto the production line
  • Connect hoses and fill heads to support filling operations
  • Operate control panels and production equipment
  • Stack, wrap and prepare pallets for dispatch
  • Move raw materials and finished products throughout the site
  • Operate forklifts and other mobile plant equipment where licensed
  • Perform routine cleaning and housekeeping duties
  • Follow quality, safety and operational procedures at all times
About You
  • Previous experience in manufacturing, production, process work or machine operation is highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Physically fit and capable of manual handling tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Reliable, punctual and safety-focused
  • Able to work effectively as part of a team
  • Forklift licence is advantageous but not essential
Requirements
  • Full working rights within Australia
  • Availability to work rotating day and afternoon shifts between 6:00am and 8:45pm
  • Current driver's licence and reliable transport
  • Ability to pass a National Police Check
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment Drug and Alcohol Screen
What's on Offer?
  • Immediate start available
  • Competitive casual hourly rate of $46 per hour + penalties 
  • Full-time hours with rotating shifts
  • Variety of duties through regular task rotation
  • Supportive team environment
  • Potential for ongoing or permanent employment for suitable candidates

job.title: Utility & Facility Manager
job.description:
Utility & Facilities Manager | Northmead, NSW
Lead facilities operations at a major industrial site while driving safety, compliance, and continuous improvement.

Our client is seeking an experienced Utility & Facilities Manager to oversee facilities management operations based in Northmead, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity for a proactive, commercially minded facilities professional who thrives in complex operational environments and enjoys building strong stakeholder relationships while delivering high standards of service, compliance, and project execution.

About the Opportunity
Reporting to the Construction Manager, you will be responsible for managing facilities operations, contractor performance, compliance requirements, and facilities-related capital projects at a key production facility.

You will work closely with operational leaders, service providers, contractors, and internal stakeholders to ensure facilities are safe, compliant, efficient, and fit for purpose.

This role offers a blend of operational facilities management, contractor governance, budget oversight, and project delivery, making it an ideal opportunity for someone looking to make a tangible impact within a large-scale manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage the performance and relationship of external Facilities Management service providers.
  • Oversee delivery of both hard and soft facilities services, including planned and reactive maintenance, cleaning, landscaping, waste management, pest control, and statutory compliance.
  • Ensure facilities and building infrastructure are maintained safely, efficiently, and cost effectively.
  • Coordinate contractor activities and manage permit-to-work processes.
  • Monitor and drive compliance with health, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead facilities-related continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Provide regular reporting on facilities performance, budgets, risks, and project delivery.
  • Monitor operational expenditure and identify opportunities to improve value and cost efficiencies.
  • Manage minor capital works projects from planning and procurement through to completion and handover.
  • Partner with site leadership teams to support operational continuity and business objectives.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Proven experience managing facilities management contracts, service providers, and contractors.
  • Experience delivering capital works projects within manufacturing, industrial, logistics, or commercial environments.
  • Strong knowledge of contractor management, permit-to-work systems, and workplace health and safety requirements.
  • Demonstrated budget management and cost-control experience.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Strong understanding of the National Construction Code (BCA) and relevant Australian Standards.
  • Qualifications in Facilities Management, Construction, Project Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills.
  • A current Australian Driver's Licence and full Australian working rights.
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to lead facilities operations at a major manufacturing site.
  • Exposure to complex industrial environments and infrastructure projects.
  • Ownership of capital projects and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborative and supportive stakeholder environment.
  • Career growth within a well-established and highly regarded organisation.
  • Competitive remuneration package.

job.title: Group Finance Manager
job.description:
Group Finance Manager, Multi-Entity Private Group
Campbelfield 

Our client is a privately owned, founder-led group of businesses with a combined annual turnover exceeding $30 million. The Group spans six operating entities across bin hire and property development, waste services, legal services, agriculture and wellness, all wholly owned by a single Director who moves fast and runs multiple projects at once.

This is not a conventional Group Finance Manager role. It's a genuine seat at the table with a founder who has built serious value across his businesses but knows his financial oversight hasn't kept pace with growth. Fund flows between entities haven't always been formally documented, and there's currently no single consolidated view of the Group's debt, cash or net asset position.

You'll be the first person to sit across the entire Group with a clear mandate: bring order, structure and visibility to the Director's complete financial position, business and personal.

Responsibilities
  • Owning the Group's consolidated financial position at all times, with the Director able to get an accurate answer to any financial question within the hour
  • Managing everything from personal expenses through to major capital requirements for property acquisitions and construction
  • Rolling cash flow forecasts and a weekly cash and debt summary for the Director
  • Overseeing the bookkeeping team and liaising with the external tax agent on compliance
  • Building and enforcing clear financial controls, including a formal intercompany transfer process
  • Supporting evaluation of new property acquisitions, including development feasibility modelling
  • Managing banking relationships and lender communication across a large number of accounts
What We're Looking For:
  • 7+ years in a senior finance role, ideally across multiple entities or a group structure
  • Comfortable working directly with a founder where priorities shift fast; you're a stabilising force, not an extra variable
  • Advanced Xero skills across multiple entities, without needing support
  • Experience managing or directing bookkeepers and junior finance staff
  • CPA or CA preferred, though exceptional experience will be considered in place of it
  • Absolute discretion; you'll have full visibility of the Director's personal and business financial position
Why This Role:

 At 30 days, you'll have delivered a complete financial map of the Group. At 6 months, clear controls are in place and the Director gets a weekly summary he can rely on. At 12 months, you're his most trusted operational partner, contributing directly to decisions on acquisitions, cash deployment and growth.

This is a genuinely broad, high-trust mandate for someone who wants ownership, not just oversight.

To apply, submit your CV along with a short cover note on why this particular role, its pace, complexity and scope, appeals to you.

job.title: Support Needs Assessors
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Support Needs Assessors to join a Federal Government client on a full-time contract. In this role, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred assessments, working directly with participants to identify and articulate their support needs in a clear, evidence-based and respectful manner.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct support needs assessments with participants and their representatives
  • Analyse information and external evidence to support sound, evidence-based decisions
  • Prepare clear, accurate assessment reports
  • Communicate assessment processes and outcomes clearly (virtual and face-to-face)
  • Apply relevant policies, procedures and legislative frameworks
  • Identify and escalate complex or high-risk matters
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support participant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records using case management systems
  • Adapt assessment approaches to suit individual participant needs
About You You will bring:

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience in assessment, interviewing or case management
  • Ability to interpret evidence and provide clear, defensible recommendations
  • A commitment to person-centred, inclusive and trauma-informed practice
  • Sound judgement, professionalism and ethical integrity
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Experience working within or knowledge of NDIS or similar frameworks (highly regarded)
Essential Requirements
  • Recognised tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, such as:

    • Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech Pathology
    • Social Work, Counselling, Psychology/Psychotherapy
    • Exercise Physiology, Dietetics, Rehabilitation Counselling
    • Nursing (RN/EN), Education-qualified clinicians
    • NDIS Behaviour Support Practitioner
  • Experience in support needs assessments or similar frameworks

  • Understanding of person-centred and strengths-based approaches

For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com 

If you fit the above criteria we would love to hear from you, APPLY now!

job.title: Catering Attendant EOI
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking Expressions of Interest from reliable, hardworking Catering Attendants / Potwash to support our client’s industrial catering team based in Adelaide’s western suburbs.

These opportunities may suit people looking for ongoing and regular work in a clean, inclusive onsite environment, with onsite parking, full uniform, and meals provided.

Key responsibilities
  • Sorting and packing catering equipment
  • Fast-paced food preparation and meal plating
  • Repetitive manual handling and packing duties
  • General cleaning and hygiene tasks
  • Washing/cleaning equipment including cutlery and dishes
To be considered, you will ideally have
  • Recent, relevant experience in food manufacturing / high-volume food environments
  • Strong knowledge of food hygiene practices and quality standards
  • Good literacy and numeracy skills
  • Ability to pass a full medical and National Police Clearance
  • Flexibility to work day and afternoon shifts across a 7-day roster
  • Reliable car and licence
  • Full working rights and strong availability
  • Proven reliability, initiative, and strong work ethic
Important: This role does not count towards the 88 days requirement for a Working Holiday Visa.

How to register your interest If you’re available for an immediate start and would like to be considered as shifts become available, please click APPLY NOW and upload your resume. A consultant will be in touch after reviewing your application.

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:
  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

job.title: Support Needs Assessors
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Support Needs Assessors to join a Federal Government client on a full-time contract. In this role, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred assessments, working directly with participants to identify and articulate their support needs in a clear, evidence-based and respectful manner.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct support needs assessments with participants and their representatives
  • Analyse information and external evidence to support sound, evidence-based decisions
  • Prepare clear, accurate assessment reports
  • Communicate assessment processes and outcomes clearly (virtual and face-to-face)
  • Apply relevant policies, procedures and legislative frameworks
  • Identify and escalate complex or high-risk matters
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support participant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records using case management systems
  • Adapt assessment approaches to suit individual participant needs
About You You will bring:

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience in assessment, interviewing or case management
  • Ability to interpret evidence and provide clear, defensible recommendations
  • A commitment to person-centred, inclusive and trauma-informed practice
  • Sound judgement, professionalism and ethical integrity
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Experience working within or knowledge of NDIS or similar frameworks (highly regarded)
Essential Requirements
  • Recognised tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, such as:

    • Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech Pathology
    • Social Work, Counselling, Psychology/Psychotherapy
    • Exercise Physiology, Dietetics, Rehabilitation Counselling
    • Nursing (RN/EN), Education-qualified clinicians
    • NDIS Behaviour Support Practitioner
  • Experience in support needs assessments or similar frameworks

  • Understanding of person-centred and strengths-based approaches

job.title: OT Technical Business Analyst
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced OT Technical Business Analyst to join our client AGL on a large-scale technology and operational transformation program. This is an exciting opportunity to work within a complex Operational Technology (OT) environment, partnering with business and technical stakeholders to deliver critical technology solutions that support operational assets and infrastructure. Based in Melbourne CBD, this contract is available for an immediate start through to June 2027 in a hybrid working environment. 

About the Role
As the OT Technical Business Analyst, you will play a key role in bridging the gap between business requirements and technical solution delivery. Working closely with project teams, architects, engineers, and operational stakeholders, you will ensure requirements are accurately captured, validated, and translated into effective solutions.
You will contribute across the full project lifecycle, supporting analysis, solution design, testing, change management, and operational readiness activities. 

About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience as a Business Analyst within Operational Technology (OT), industrial systems, utilities, manufacturing or critical infrastructure environments
  • Strong requirements gathering, process mapping and business analysis capabilities
  • Understanding of OT technologies including SCADA, PLC and DCS environments
  • Experience working across OT and IT integration initiatives
  • Strong knowledge of business process modelling and requirements management frameworks
  • Experience using tools such as JIRA, Confluence, Visio and BPMN modelling tools
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, facilitation and communication skills
  • Experience working within Agile, Hybrid or Waterfall project environments
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with a high attention to detail
  • Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline.

job.title: HR/ER Advisor
job.description:
HR / Employee Relations Advisor

FIFO from Perth | 8/6 Days-Only Roster | 6-Month Initial Contract | Immediate Start

We are currently seeking an experienced HR / Employee Relations Advisor to join a busy mining operation on a FIFO basis from Perth. This is an excellent opportunity for a hands-on HR professional who enjoys supporting frontline leaders, driving performance management outcomes, and ensuring compliance with workplace policies and Fair Work processes.

This role is heavily focused on administration, documentation, and coaching leaders, providing practical support to supervisors and superintendents while allowing them to focus on operational priorities in the field.

Key Responsibilities
  • Partner with Superintendents and operational leaders to establish a consistent baseline approach to performance management across site.
  • Coach and support supervisors in managing performance, attendance, behavioural, and conduct-related issues.

job.title: Operations Manager (Owner's Representative)
job.description:
Our client is delivering a first-of-its-kind minerals processing facility in North Queensland, supporting the advancement and commercialisation of critical minerals. As the project transitions from construction into commissioning and early operations, they are seeking an experienced Operations Manager (Owner's Representative) to act as the owner's on-site representative and oversee operational governance, stakeholder coordination and readiness activities. 


About the Role
This is a site-based position in Townsville, working at the centre of a brand-new processing facility as it moves toward commissioning and operational readiness.

Unlike a traditional Plant Manager role, this position is not responsible for running the plant day-to-day or managing operational teams. Instead, you will act as the owner's representative, working closely with the contracted operator, suppliers, customers and stakeholders to ensure the facility operates safely, reliably and in line with the owner's expectations. 

This role is ideally suited to someone with strong stakeholder management, governance and operational assurance capability, coupled with the technical credibility to engage with complex processing operations and challenge outcomes when required. 


Key Responsibilities
  • Represent the asset owner on-site and oversee operator performance
  • Establish and maintain operational governance and assurance frameworks
  • Coordinate commissioning readiness, campaign readiness and early operations activities
  • Monitor operational performance, KPIs, incidents and corrective actions
  • Provide oversight of safety systems, critical controls and high-risk activities
  • Maintain governance over Management of Change (MOC) and asset configuration
  • Support strategic asset reliability and lifecycle management initiatives
  • Act as the key interface between operators, suppliers, customers, contractors and government stakeholders
  • Prepare executive briefings, recommendations and operational reports
  • Support procurement, contracts and commercial service delivery activities

About You
  • Experience within minerals processing, resources, energy, chemicals, heavy industry, infrastructure or other complex industrial environments
  • Exposure to commissioning, start-up, operational readiness or facility transitions
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management capability
  • Proven ability to influence outcomes without direct line authority
  • Experience in operational governance, assurance, asset management and Management of Change (MOC) 
  • Strong understanding of maintenance planning and asset management systems such as SAP or similar CMMS platforms 
  • Comfortable operating in an ambiguous, first-of-its-kind environment where priorities continue to evolve
  • Previous Owner's Representative, Operational Assurance, Asset Management or Governance experience will be highly regarded 

What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to shape a brand-new processing facility during commissioning and early operations
  • Unique owner-side role focused on governance, assurance and stakeholder leadership
  • Significant autonomy and influence without direct operational management responsibilities
  • Potential relocation support available for interstate candidates
  • 38-hour work week (Monday-Friday)
  • AO8 Level, approximately $100/hr + super
  • Long-term project through to June 2028
  • Backing of a major Queensland Government initiative

job.description:
Are you passionate about optimising infrastructure assets and driving organisational excellence? We’re seeking a talented Infrastructure Asset Management Specialist to join our client and deliver strategic outcomes that make a real difference. This is an initial 9-month contract with strong extension potential, offering an exciting opportunity to lead key asset management initiatives within a dynamic, asset-intensive environment, shaping the future of organisational asset practices and standards.

Collaborating with internal teams and external stakeholders, you'll develop and implement asset management strategies in line with ISO 55000 standards, ensuring continuous improvement and organisational capability uplift.

The successful candidate will possess proven experience in infrastructure asset management, with a track record of leading complex projects from inception to successful implementation. You will bring strong analytical, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement skills, capable of translating technical insights into practical business improvements. Your familiarity with asset data standards, governance frameworks, and lifecycle management will be vital in influencing positive change and driving asset performance.

job.title: High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator
job.description:
High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator
Chadstone, VIC
$125,000 + 12% Superannuation
Permanent Full-Time
Onsite Position

Operating a purpose-built training facility, our client plays a vital role in developing apprentices, tradespeople and industry professionals across the energy, rail and major infrastructure sectors. Supporting training in power distribution, transmission and other critical industries, they are committed to maintaining a safe, compliant and industry-leading learning environment. Due to continued growth and operational requirements, an opportunity has become available for a High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator to join their team at their Chadstone facility.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced electrical professional to take ownership of safety, compliance and operational readiness across a specialised high-voltage training environment.
Working closely with trainers, contractors, industry stakeholders and safety teams, you will coordinate electrical safety systems, permits, inspections and maintenance activities while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, regulations and industry standards.
In this role, you will play a key part in supporting the safe operation, maintenance and compliance of high-voltage and electrical training assets, helping to create a safe and effective environment for staff, students, apprentices and visitors.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate the safe operation and use of high voltage and electrical training assets.
  • Administer and maintain permit-to-work systems, including Electrical Access Permits and excavation permits.
  • Maintain safety documentation including authorisations, competency records, inductions and compliance registers.
  • Coordinate planned and reactive maintenance activities across training infrastructure.
  • Manage inspections and ensure corrective actions and remediation works are completed.
  • Support ongoing compliance with Victorian electrical safety legislation, regulations and industry requirements.
  • Facilitate contractor and visitor inductions and ensure site compliance requirements are met.
  • Work collaboratively with trainers, operational teams and industry stakeholders to identify and manage risk.
  • Assist with the development, implementation and continuous improvement of safety management systems.
  • Liaise with regulatory bodies, contractors and industry partners as required.
  • Support a safe learning environment for apprentices, students, staff and visitors.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Experience within electrical, utilities, infrastructure, energy or other high-risk operational environments.
  • Sound knowledge of electrical safety legislation, compliance requirements and safe work practices.
  • Experience managing permit systems, safety procedures and compliance documentation.
  • Knowledge of high voltage operations, switching, isolation procedures and access permit requirements.
  • Experience coordinating maintenance activities, inspections and risk management processes.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Excellent organisational, communication and record-keeping abilities.
  • A proactive and collaborative approach to safety and compliance.
Essential Requirements
  • Current ESI licence, electrical trade qualification or equivalent recognised qualification relevant to the role.
  • Demonstrated experience in electrical safety and compliance environments.
  • Strong knowledge of permit-to-work systems and safety management processes.
  • Valid Victorian Working with Children Check, or willingness to obtain one prior to commencement.
  • Full Australian working rights.
Desirable
  • Current or previous High Voltage Authorisation.
  • Experience within electricity distribution, transmission, rail, utilities or training environments.
  • Experience working with Energy Safe Victoria requirements or similar regulatory frameworks.
What's on Offer
  • $125,000 + 12% Superannuation.
  • Permanent full-time opportunity.
  • Stable, onsite role based in Chadstone.
  • Opportunity to work within a specialised high-voltage training environment.
  • Broad stakeholder engagement across industry, contractors and regulatory bodies.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • A meaningful role helping develop the future workforce of Australia's energy and infrastructure sectors.
Additional Information
The successful candidate will be required to complete a National Police Check as part of the pre-employment process.

Apply Now If you're an experienced electrical safety, compliance or high-voltage professional looking to leverage your technical expertise in a unique and purpose-driven environment, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Confidence presenting information to both individuals and small groups
  • Strong computer literacy and the ability to navigate multiple systems simultaneously
  • High attention to detail and strong organisational skills
  • Ability to build rapport quickly with people from diverse backgrounds
  • A customer service mindset with a professional and friendly approach
  • Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to prioritise competing tasks and meet deadlines

You'll enjoy:

job.title: Technical Officer - Chemistry Laboratories
job.description:
100% Onsite | Contract until 18 October

We are seeking an experienced Technical Officer to support the safe and effective operation of chemistry-aligned laboratories within a STEM teaching and research environment.

Working alongside the Technical Coordinator, you will oversee day-to-day laboratory operations while providing specialist technical support to staff, students and researchers. This is a hands-on role covering chemical and equipment management, compressed gases, laboratory safety, maintenance, documentation and technical training.

The Role
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing the day-to-day operation of chemistry-aligned laboratories and technical workspaces
  • Safely transporting, connecting and managing compressed gas cylinders
  • Managing chemicals, chemical inventories and chemical waste
  • Maintaining laboratory consumables, stock levels and purchasing requirements
  • Managing specialist laboratory equipment, including access, servicing, routine maintenance and calibration
  • Developing and maintaining SOPs, Safe Work Instructions, risk assessments, chemical registers and other laboratory documentation
  • Providing technical advice, training and laboratory inductions to students, staff and other users
  • Developing preventative maintenance schedules and ensuring equipment remains operational and available
  • Supporting safe laboratory practices and ensuring compliance with relevant OH&S legislation, standards and organisational procedures
  • Identifying safety or compliance issues and supporting the development and implementation of remediation plans
  • Maintaining laboratories and workspaces in a clean, safe and operational condition
  • Assisting with the acquisition, installation and commissioning of new laboratory equipment and resources
  • Working closely with technical, teaching and research stakeholders to support planned laboratory activities

About You
We are looking for someone with strong practical laboratory experience who is comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day technical operations.
You will ideally bring:
  • Demonstrated experience working within chemistry, chemical engineering or a related laboratory environment
  • Extensive experience with the safe handling, transport and connection of compressed gas cylinders
  • Strong experience managing chemicals and chemical waste
  • Experience working with and maintaining specialised or custom chemical laboratory equipment
  • Previous laboratory operations and maintenance experience, ideally within a teaching or research environment
  • A sound understanding of OH&S legislation, laboratory safety requirements and relevant industry standards
  • Experience developing or maintaining SOPs, risk assessments and safe working documentation
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to laboratory operations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders

Qualifications & Requirements
  • Tertiary qualification in Chemistry or a related discipline, and/or substantial relevant laboratory experience
  • Experience within the tertiary education or research sector will be highly regarded
  • A valid Victorian Working with Children Check is mandatory

If you’re an experienced laboratory professional with a strong chemistry background who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with safety, equipment management and supporting teaching and research, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: MR Truck Driver / Forklift Operator
job.description:
MR Truck Driver / Forklift Operator
Our client is seeking a reliable and experienced MR Truck Driver / Forklift Operator to join the team within the fruit and vegetable packaging industry.
This is a hands-on role combining local deliveries, forklift operation, and warehouse support activities. You will be responsible for completing deliveries throughout Adelaide's northern suburbs and surrounding market garden regions while assisting with loading, unloading, and general warehouse duties when required. This position offers consistent year-round employment, with significantly increased hours and overtime opportunities during the busy summer produce season.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Complete local deliveries throughout Adelaide's northern suburbs and surrounding market garden regions.
  • Safely load and unload trucks using a forklift and manual handling techniques.
  • Verify customer orders, delivery documentation, and product quantities before dispatch.
  • Ensure goods are delivered accurately and professionally to customers.
  • Secure loads and transport products safely.
  • Maintain trucks, forklifts, and warehouse areas to a high standard.
  • Assist with warehouse operations, order preparation, and general site duties.
  • Report equipment faults, delivery issues, or safety concerns promptly.
  • Follow all workplace health and safety procedures and company policies.
  • Support the wider team during peak operational periods.
 
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • Current MR License (or higher).
  • Current LF Forklift License.
  • Previous truck driving and forklift operating experience.
  • Experience loading and unloading vehicles safely.
  • Strong time management and organisational skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage daily delivery schedules.
  • Good customer service and communication skills.
  • Understanding of load restraint and safe manual handling practices.
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety.
 
Working Hours
As part of the fresh produce industry, this role operates within a seasonal environment, and working hours will vary throughout the year based on customer demand and operational requirements.
During the winter season, employees can expect a minimum of approximately 28-30 hours per week.
During the summer peak season, working hours increase significantly, with regular overtime opportunities available. Saturday work may also be required during busy periods.
 
 
What's On Offer?
  • Competitive pay rate of $35.40 per hour
  • Consistent year-round employment
  • Overtime opportunities during peak season
  • Supportive team environment
  • Diverse role combining driving, forklift operation, and warehouse duties
  • Opportunity to become a valued long-term member of the team
 
Why Apply?
This role is ideal for someone who understands that being a driver is more than simply driving a truck. We are looking for a team player who is willing to assist wherever required, takes pride in their work, and provides excellent service to customers while maintaining a strong focus on safety.
If you are a dependable MR Truck Driver / Forklift Operator looking for a varied and rewarding role with additional earning potential during the busy summer season, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Investment Planning Analyst (Housing & Grid Infrastructure)
job.description:
Senior Investment Planning Analyst
Housing & Grid Infrastructure

Drive the planning and investment decisions that support Western Australia's future growth.

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Investment Planning Analyst to play a key role in shaping major network infrastructure investment programs that support housing development, grid optimisation, and long-term network performance.

This is a highly visible position that combines strategic planning, portfolio management, financial forecasting, and stakeholder engagement. While advertised as a Senior Investment Planning Analyst, the successful candidate will operate as a Senior Grid Portfolio Analyst, responsible for developing investment plans, managing project pipelines, forecasting expenditure, and supporting critical network infrastructure programs.

About the Role
Working across large-scale housing and grid infrastructure portfolios, you will help ensure the right projects are planned, prioritised, funded, and delivered at the right time. You will provide valuable insights that support investment decisions, network capacity planning, and long-term infrastructure strategy.

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio management teams while contributing to major infrastructure initiatives that support growing communities across Western Australia.

Key Responsibilities
Portfolio & Investment Planning
  • Develop and maintain short and long-term investment plans across housing and grid optimisation portfolios.
  • Build and manage multi-year project pipelines aligned with strategic network objectives.
  • Identify project dependencies, approval pathways, critical milestones, and delivery risks.
  • Support annual planning cycles and long-term network investment strategies.
Budgeting & Forecasting
  • Develop and maintain portfolio budgets and expenditure forecasts.
  • Translate capital investment plans into accurate monthly and annual financial forecasts.
  • Maintain rolling expenditure forecasts and analyse variances against budget.
  • Provide recommendations and insights to support investment decision-making.
Housing & Infrastructure Program Planning
  • Monitor infrastructure requirements associated with housing growth initiatives.
  • Analyse network capacity, anticipated housing developments, and energisation timelines.
  • Assess future investment requirements and identify potential capacity constraints.
  • Develop planning scenarios to support prioritisation and risk assessment.
Project Pipeline Management
  • Maintain a forward-looking portfolio of infrastructure projects.
  • Support resource planning, investment prioritisation, and governance processes.
  • Monitor project readiness and ensure key approvals are achieved within required timeframes.
  • Track delivery risks and emerging portfolio challenges.
Stakeholder Engagement & Reporting
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders across planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio teams.
  • Produce reports, forecasts, and analysis for senior leaders and decision-makers.
  • Develop tools, dashboards, and reporting processes that improve planning accuracy and visibility.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across forecasting and portfolio management practices.
About You
  • Experience managing investment plans, project portfolios, infrastructure programs, or complex project schedules.
  • Strong financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical capabilities.
  • The ability to interpret complex data and translate it into meaningful business insights.
  • Experience balancing multiple priorities, dependencies, resources, and delivery timelines.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate risks and provide practical recommendations.
  • Advanced Excel and data analysis capability, with experience using planning and reporting tools.
  • Experience within utilities, infrastructure, energy, transport, resources, or other asset-intensive environments highly regarded.
Why Apply? This is an opportunity to join a high-performing team where your work will directly influence major infrastructure investment decisions. You'll play a critical role in ensuring future housing developments and network infrastructure programs are supported by sound planning, robust forecasting, and effective portfolio management.

If you're an experienced portfolio, planning, or investment professional looking to make a meaningful impact on large-scale infrastructure programs, we would love to hear from you.

Contact Centre Representative
Location: Newcastle & hybrid once trained
Contract: Casual contract, long term for right candidate
Shifts: Monday-Friday with optional Saturday once trained
 
Broaden your customer service skills and gain top notch industry knowledge within a fast-paced yet supportive call-centre environment!

Chandler Macleod’s Business Support team are looking for dynamic contact centre representatives to join an iconic employer of choice in the Newcastle region.

Hunter Water is dedicated to delivering essential services including drinking water, wastewater, recycled water, and some stormwater management to more than 600,000 residents and businesses across the Lower Hunter region.  They strive to be a forward-thinking business that operates with vision and purpose. It's an exciting time to be part of their team.
  • Work for an organisation renowned for its excellent supportive team environment & brilliant work culture
  • Hybrid arrangements + modern harbourside offices
  • Opportunity to transition to permanent employment
  • $1500 bonus on transition to permanent!

About the role
As an experienced Contact Centre Representative, you are people-orientated and adaptable, with outstanding problem-solving skills. By applying knowledge, empathy and professionalism you will assess and fulfil customer needs as the first line of support through the Contact Centre.

Being a constant point of contact for customers, you can create and/or completely transform a customer’s experience. For this reason, it is important that you are approachable, friendly and well-informed with a passion for assisting people in times of need.

 To be successful in this role, you will:
  • Provide consistently high-quality customer service by interpreting and resolving first-contact enquiries across voice, digital, and email channels. This includes face to face interactions across the Customer Service centre.
  • Recognise and navigate the complexities in customer enquiries, identifying nuanced situations that may not fit into clear-cut categories.
  • Exceed customer expectations by proactively seeking opportunities to enhance their experience.
  • Identify and escalate more complex enquiries and transactions to ensure the timely and effective resolution of issues, providing regular updates to the customer.
  • Take an active interest in the Contact Centre and individual performance to achieve customer satisfaction and performance targets
  • Participate in regular quality assessments and in operational and performance discussions.
  • Actively engage in and support continuous improvement process within the Contact Centre
  • Effectively use a range of systems, technology and telephony solutions to undertake work tasks, triage, refer or escalate work tasks

About you
Demonstrating a desire to learn and progress within the role, you will actively seek and embrace feedback to identify areas for growth and improve overall performance.

Naturally, you’ll bring a commitment to customer service, business improvement, Company Values and Customer Commitment along with a strong team-focused work ethic with the ability to achieve individual and group objectives.

In addition you will have:
  • Minimum 1-2 years’ experience in a contact centre or customer service role across voice, digital, email, and face-to-face channels along with proven ability to deliver first-contact resolution and meet customer service targets
  • An ability to interpret complex data and confidently translate to customers in a professional manner
  • Confident to navigate multiple systems, technology platforms, and telephony tools to source relevant information quickly
  • Willingness to commit to reliable attendance of shifts and the requirement to work from the office on scheduled days
 
If this sounds like you, and you’re ready for your next new challenge, click the “Apply” button to submit your application or call Yolande on 02 4978 7738 for more details!

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
About the Opportunity
We are currently seeking an experienced Project Manager to support the delivery of electrical infrastructure projects across Victoria.
This role sits within the electrical, utilities, and infrastructure space and would suit someone with a strong background within the electrical infrastructure and renewable energy space.

While the title is Project Manager, this is very much a hybrid role that requires someone who can comfortably bridge the gap between project management and technical delivery.
You'll be working closely with engineering, commissioning, and site teams to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and on schedule.

Projects & Work Scope
You'll be supporting the delivery of projects that may include:
  • HV substation upgrades and infrastructure projects
  • Renewable energy developments
  • Grid connection works
  • Electrical infrastructure upgrades
  • Commissioning and energisation activities
  • Network and utility-related projects
  • Brownfield and greenfield electrical works
The role will require someone who understands project delivery from both a management and technical perspective, including how engineering, construction, testing, and commissioning activities all come together.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Lead project delivery activities from initiation through to completion
  • Coordinate engineers, contractors, commissioning teams, and stakeholders
  • Manage project schedules, costs, risks, and reporting
  • Support commissioning and project handover activities
  • Work closely with site delivery and engineering teams to resolve technical challenges
  • Ensure projects are delivered safely, on time, and within budget
  • Manage stakeholder communication across clients, suppliers, and internal teams
  • Assist with procurement, planning, outage coordination, and project execution where required

To be successful, you'll ideally bring:
  • Previous experience as a Project Manager, Project Engineer, or Senior Project Engineer
  • Experience within the electrical infrastructure and renewable energy sectors would be highly regarded
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
  • Experience working across project delivery and commissioning activities
  • Ability to confidently engage with technical teams and understand engineering challenges

Why Apply?

job.description:

Location: Perth CBD
Roster: 5:2
Contract: ASAP Start | Until June 2027

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Planner to support a major decarbonisation program involving renewable energy infrastructure, electrification initiatives, battery-electric mining fleets, OEM development programs and operational transition activities.
This role will be responsible for developing, maintaining and optimising integrated project schedules across a diverse portfolio of capital projects, ensuring successful delivery from concept and engineering through to commissioning, operational readiness and handover.
Working within a high-performing project services team, you will collaborate closely with project delivery, engineering, procurement, operations, contractors and OEM partners to provide schedule leadership, performance analysis and project controls support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain integrated master schedules and detailed project schedules across multiple decarbonisation projects.
  • Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, fleet readiness and operational transition activities within portfolio schedules.
  • Develop resource, commodity and cost-loaded schedules.
  • Perform critical path analysis, milestone tracking and "what-if" scenario planning.
  • Maintain schedule integrity through logic reviews, schedule health checks and planning best practices.
  • Implement Earned Value Management (EVM) and analyse schedule performance, including CPI and SPI reporting.
  • Review and integrate contractor, supplier and OEM schedules into master project programs.
  • Identify schedule risks, opportunities and emerging trends, providing proactive recommendations to project teams.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly progress, performance and forecasting reports.
  • Participate in schedule reviews, risk workshops, change management processes and capital planning activities.
About You
Essential Experience
  • Minimum 10 years' experience in project planning and scheduling.
  • Proven client-side experience across the full project lifecycle, from concept through to execution and handover.
  • Experience supporting major capital projects within mining, resources, energy, infrastructure or industrial sectors.
  • Strong understanding of project controls, scheduling methodologies and project governance.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating multiple contractor, supplier and operational schedules.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Strong commitment to health, safety and environmental standards.
Technical Skills
  • Advanced Primavera P6 experience.
  • Strong Microsoft Office Suite skills.
  • Experience using Power BI or similar reporting and business intelligence tools.
  • Sound understanding of Earned Value Management (EVM) principles and performance reporting.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability.
Desirable Qualifications
  • Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Project Management or a related discipline.
  • Project Controls, Planning or Scheduling certification.
  • Experience in mining fleet electrification, OEM programs or decarbonisation initiatives.
What's on Offer
  • ASAP start

  • Develop, maintain and implement documentation including SOPs, Safe Work Instructions, equipment risk assessments and chemical registers.
  • Provide technical advice, guidance and training to laboratory users, including conducting and documenting inductions.
  • Support the purchasing of equipment, instruments, consumables and other laboratory requirements.

About You
You will be a proactive and highly organised laboratory professional with strong technical knowledge and a practical approach to problem solving.
To be successful, you will have:
  • Extensive experience using and maintaining general laboratory instrumentation within a research environment.
  • Experience working with compressed gases, including connections, handling and safe transportation.
  • Experience with glovebox facilities.
  • Knowledge of chemicals and biological materials, including appropriate waste disposal processes.
  • Proven experience working within a chemistry, chemical engineering, physics or related laboratory environment.
  • Previous laboratory operations and maintenance experience, ideally within a teaching, research or higher education environment.

In this role, you will be responsible for delivering project outcomes across HSE, quality, cost and schedule, while managing internal and external resources to support safe, controlled execution across the full project lifecycle—from front-end studies through to construction, commissioning and close-out.

Location: Perth metro office-based in 2026, with site travel as required (no FIFO)
Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Start:  Target early September
Rates: Will reflect your level of expertise

This brownfields upgrade forms part of a broader growth program and includes:
  • Processing plant upgrade modifications
  • Procurement and installation of a new SAG ball crushing mill
  • Feeder bin and DSM screens
  • Early works and long-lead items that have already been funded and approved

job.title: Project Assurance Officer

This role is ideal for a governance, assurance, risk, or project management professional who enjoys analysing project performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting successful project delivery outcomes.

Working under limited direction, you will play an important role in supporting project governance and assurance activities across a diverse project portfolio, ensuring projects are delivered in alignment with established frameworks, standards, and organisational objectives.



About the Role As a Project Assurance Officer, you will contribute to the oversight and continuous improvement of project delivery by conducting assurance activities, reviewing project documentation and reporting, identifying emerging risks and issues, and providing evidence-based advice to project teams and senior stakeholders.
You will work closely with project managers, governance bodies, and subject matter experts to strengthen project management practices and support informed decision-making across a complex portfolio of work.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct project assurance activities in line with established frameworks, processes, and standards.
  • Review project documentation, governance arrangements, schedules, budgets, risks, issues, benefits, and reporting artefacts.
  • Analyse project performance information and assurance evidence to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefs, governance papers, dashboards, and recommendations for senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Support executive oversight through the provision of clear, evidence-based advice.
  • Build productive relationships with project managers, senior responsible officers, and key stakeholders.
  • Contribute to the improvement of project governance, assurance frameworks, templates, guidance material, and reporting processes.
  • Support the coordination of governance forums, including agenda preparation, action tracking, decision registers, and follow-up activities.
  • Escalate emerging risks, issues, and areas of non-compliance where required.
  • Promote consistent project management practices and support capability uplift initiatives across project teams.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, reporting, evaluation, or a related discipline.
  • Sound understanding of project lifecycle management, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, scheduling, benefits management, reporting, and assurance practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret information from multiple sources and identify key risks and insights.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with experience preparing briefs, reports, committee papers, dashboards, and executive-level advice.
  • Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

job.title: Project Assurance Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Project Assurance Officer to join a Federal Government client on a contract opportunity. This role is ideal for a governance, assurance, risk, or project management professional who enjoys analysing project performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting successful project delivery outcomes.

Working under limited direction, you will play an important role in supporting project governance and assurance activities across a diverse project portfolio, ensuring projects are delivered in alignment with established frameworks, standards, and organisational objectives.



About the Role As a Project Assurance Officer, you will contribute to the oversight and continuous improvement of project delivery by conducting assurance activities, reviewing project documentation and reporting, identifying emerging risks and issues, and providing evidence-based advice to project teams and senior stakeholders.
You will work closely with project managers, governance bodies, and subject matter experts to strengthen project management practices and support informed decision-making across a complex portfolio of work.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct project assurance activities in line with established frameworks, processes, and standards.
  • Review project documentation, governance arrangements, schedules, budgets, risks, issues, benefits, and reporting artefacts.
  • Analyse project performance information and assurance evidence to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefs, governance papers, dashboards, and recommendations for senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Support executive oversight through the provision of clear, evidence-based advice.
  • Build productive relationships with project managers, senior responsible officers, and key stakeholders.
  • Contribute to the improvement of project governance, assurance frameworks, templates, guidance material, and reporting processes.
  • Support the coordination of governance forums, including agenda preparation, action tracking, decision registers, and follow-up activities.
  • Escalate emerging risks, issues, and areas of non-compliance where required.
  • Promote consistent project management practices and support capability uplift initiatives across project teams.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, reporting, evaluation, or a related discipline.
  • Sound understanding of project lifecycle management, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, scheduling, benefits management, reporting, and assurance practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret information from multiple sources and identify key risks and insights.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with experience preparing briefs, reports, committee papers, dashboards, and executive-level advice.
  • Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to build and maintain productive working relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Sound judgement, initiative, and the ability to work independently while managing competing priorities.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate, quality outcomes within deadlines.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and enhancing governance and assurance practices.
Highly Desirable
  • Experience supporting governance committees, project assurance reviews, portfolio reporting, or enterprise project management functions.
  • Experience contributing to project capability uplift initiatives, process improvement activities, or assurance frameworks.
  • Qualifications or training in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, business analysis, evaluation, or related fields.
Security Requirements

If you have a passion for project governance, assurance, and continuous improvement, we encourage you to apply today.

job.description:
